For x=4s, choose the root U(s)≡1 mod 8 of 1+16s²/b: v↦v+4v² is an isometry and bijective on each finite quotient. The square-root difference identity gives U(s)−U(t) divisible by 8(s−t); thus s↦sU(s) is an isometry, bijective on all finite quotients and hence on Z₂. The third branch is exactly a²+16b times the square image translated by a² (i.e. a²+16b S₂). Reducing the three images mod 8 gives 2−3a, 5, 1; coincidences are absorptions into the first, full ball. Unit squares have measure 1/8, and the valuations of nonzero squares are even, giving square measure 1/6 by summing 4⁻ʲ/8.
